Chapter Four: Race, Colorism, and the Complexities of Belonging
Living between worlds, you can’t help but notice how race shapes every aspect of life. In a new country, skin color instantly sets you apart—sometimes it’s a source of pride, but often it brings pain. Being Black isn’t just an identity; it’s an experience molded by history, by stereotypes, and by the everyday reality of discrimination.
But here’s something we don’t always talk about: even within the same community, divisions exist. Colorism, class differences, and the lingering effects of colonialism all create layers of hierarchy—some obvious, some quietly hidden in daily interactions.
And then there’s the pressure—constant, exhausting—to fit into Western ideas of beauty. Lighter skin, straighter hair, certain features get celebrated, while others are pushed aside. The message hits hard: to truly fit in, you’re supposed to hide or even erase what makes you different. Think about the impact of that—how it shapes not just the way you see yourself, but how you connect with others. So much of it happens beneath the surface, invisible to anyone who hasn’t lived it.
Still, there’s this deep sense of pride—a connection to heritage and culture that runs strong and resilient. The challenge is holding onto that pride, even when everything around you says to let go. Racism isn’t just about the obvious acts; it’s woven into the way society operates, quietly closing doors and pushing people to the margins.
Inside families and communities, colorism leaves its own scars. Sometimes, lighter-skinned relatives get special treatment, while those with darker skin feel less valued. That kind of hurt runs deep, and the longing to belong can twist into self-doubt or even shame. Healing means facing these truths head-on—naming them, challenging them, and refusing to let them define who you are.
Most people don’t realize just how deep these struggles go, or how hard it is to stand up against the pressure to conform. The journey toward self-acceptance isn’t easy. There are moments of doubt, but also moments of real pride. Choosing to embrace your own beauty—rejecting standards that were never meant for you—isn’t just bold, it’s absolutely necessary.
Out in the world, racism keeps showing you the boundaries of belonging. Some doors just stay closed, some opportunities disappear, and people make assumptions based only on how you look. But the real challenge isn’t just survival—it’s about thriving. It’s about building spaces where differences aren’t hidden, but celebrated.
Race and colorism are tangled into everyday life, affecting every choice and every relationship. There aren’t easy answers. But these days, there’s a growing sense of solidarity—a realization that this struggle is shared by many. So, the journey toward belonging isn’t just about you. It’s a collective movement, reaching for justice, dignity, and the kind of acceptance that’s real and lasting.
